question: What screen-quality or touchscreen feedback is reported for the Galaxy S20 FE?
answer:
One reviewer described the Galaxy S20 FE's screen as poor quality with distorted colors and a pinkish-blue tint that worsens at slight angles. [6975634ae389_0]
Another reviewer said the 1080p display looks fine and that differences would only be visible with a magnifying glass or eye right up to the display. [6d0b103c4a6b_1]
A reviewer reported touchscreen issues where scrolling randomly registers as clicks, most noticeable on Instagram. [86a6b180a06c_3]
One reviewer said their initial touch sensitivity and ghost-touch issues were fixed by a software update and calibration, while another reported duplicate taps and was unsure whether a screen protector was the cause. [21b16c2eacf2_5] [790b1a7beeb9_0]

chunks.text: Poor screen quality.. This was not a defective item, it is that all Samsung Amoled screens are like this. Very poor image quality, colors distorted - lots of pinking blueish tint like a bad LED tv. At only slight angle, colors get distorted even more. Apparently, AMOLED is way worse than real OLED screen, the active matrix really makes it bad looking. Surprising that Samsung makes these amoled screens not just for their own phones, but also for other brands as well. Returned this item, bought instead a phone with real OLED screen - the image quality on it is way better!

Yes... the 1080p display looks fine. You will not be able to tell the difference unless you get a magnifying glass or put your eye right up to the display. If you are coming from the s8 or and older phone, this phone is worth picking up. *Update, I'm really satisfied with the performance of the phone. Battery life with the 120hz screen is acceptable and can still last the whole day with moderate use. The rear camera is nice but the front facing camera leaves more to be desired. The performance is definitely there with the Snapdragon 865 and 6gb of ram. I used to use a phone with 8gb of ram and I don't notice a difference (I always have multiple apps open). My original opinion still stands. There have also been reports of touchscreen issues. This has not affected me.

Touch screen is REALLY glitchy (rarely works). Not a good phone. Does not stand up to other samsungs. Has a lot of glitches that just aren't getting addressed by samsung because its the cheapo version. the touchscreen works maybe 15% of the time. the rest of the time it is "lights on but nobody home." the fingerprint reader is absolutely awful. even when the touchscreen is having a good day, the finger print reader never works (it's also in an awkward place). nothing fancy about the screen, functions, or camera. overall very unhappy with it.

Overall good phone but for over a year Samsung has not fixed faulty touchscreen. This phone is a great value for the price with solid performance in basically every area except for one: the touchscreen during keyboard swiping. Swiping on the screen often registers incorrectly multiple quick touches and THEN what's left of the swipe. Needless to say, this poses problems for multiple apps but none worse than trying to type on the keyboard (3rd party keyboards don't fix the problem).

Came with a low quality replacement screen with uneven surface. Phone arrived with off-brand but functional charger and cheap stiff cable, in non-samsung box, but the possibility of this is disclosed in the description. The phone is totally pristine, including the back panel and frame, which makes me suspect aftermarket replacement which means likely poor water resistance. But it is a refurbished phone- this is not misleading or wrong. The screen is absolutely aftermarket because out of the box, there was a blob of blue adhesive near the speaker grill that I had to cut off with a knife. It functions okay, I don't have an OEM panel to compare to but it looks pretty good. The fingerprint sensor works flawlessly. The issue is that the screen has no (or just very poor) oleophobic coating, which is supposed to repel fingerprints and make your finger glide over the screen smoothly.

Cons: No headphone jack - By far my biggest complaint with the S20 FE is the lack of a headphone jack. I don't see why it's necessary to exclude the jack on Samsung's newer phones. Seems like a ploy to get consumers to buy their overpriced wireless earbuds. I had to buy some dongles on Amazon so I could use my existing headphones. Front camera quality - While the back cameras are impressive, the front camera is less so. The selfies I took with my girlfriend were kind of washed out and overly smooth. The 32mp photos don't look any better than the 8mp ones from my Note 8. Touchscreen issues - I have had touchscreen issues where instead of scrolling the screen will randomly register it as clicks instead. Most noticeable on Instragram where it'll click on random profiles instead of scrolling.

You can register a face, but it isn’t reliable in any sense and it just doesn’t hold the bar. Odds and Ends: - Touch Sensitivity: When the device first came out in 2020 there were reports of touch sensitivity problems and instances of ghost touches. My device had this issue at first but then a software update and calibration did fix my issue of touch sensitivity. I haven’t had any issues since. But on release, it was a bit rough. I think though, the software update fixed this issue for most individuals - Under-Display Fingerprint Sensor: This device comes with an optical fingerprint sensor under the display which is kind of futuristic. But it can be hit or miss. For me, after a few software updates it is almost always pretty solid and consistent.

Touch screen can be weird at times, not sure if it's my screen protector. 5g works AT&T USA. Touchscreen can do duplicate taps semi frequently... Not sure if it's my protector or the settings etc or actually something wrong with the screen. Coming from Pixel 3a, I am disappointed a newer phone's camera isn't better... It isn't a bad camera it just sucks compared to even older pixels. SD card slot is nice to have, battery life is LONG and I'm a heavy user. 5G didn't work easily with AT&T... Took me about 4 calls with their tech team. Something seemed odd to them about the IMEI and they essentially needed to assign an IMEI that would work with their 5g network. Worked out of the box on 4g LTE with my existing sim card

Phone has touch screen and functional issues. This phone has functional and touchscreen issues. Had to be pressing several times in order for it to recognize the touch, it has functional issues even after the phone is updated and overall was not a good experience. It felt like an old phone though ut was brand new. Very frustrating! Not recommended.

A lot of issues. Returning my Samsung s20 FE 5g. Maybe I just got lemon, but my phone got frozen screen 5,6 times in first two weeks and than reboots, not acceptable for new phone and 6gig ram. Also fingerprint reader is horrible, face unlock works good though. Battery life not what expected for 4500mh. Touchscreen is not always responsive, especially on the corners of the screen. Thing that I liked is great display/resolution. I would stay away from this phone, on paper everything seems amazing, in reality too many issues.
